builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Silent Instrument Errors Reorder Agent Leaderboards
summary: Replaces implicit trust in leaderboard scores and their underlying evaluation pipelines with explicit auditing of grading, logging, replay, and versioning artifacts, plus adopting four cheap checks (graded fraction, root-span cost aggregation, action provenance tagging, pinned evaluator versions with re-grade diffs). Costs are primarily engineering time to implement reporting and provenance tracking and occasional re-grading compute; no foundation-model training or cluster is required. Failure after adoption includes residual silent instrumentation bugs elsewhere, misinterpretation of published diffs or provenance, and re-grading itself becoming a new, unacknowledged measurement if versions and procedures are not pinned.
rationale: This is directly applicable to production agent evaluation on constrained infrastructure because it prevents costly decisions based on silent measurement errors by adding low-cost reporting and versioning checks.
technique: Agent evaluation instrumentation auditing and cheap checks

claims.statement: Replaces implicit trust in leaderboard scores and their underlying evaluation pipelines with explicit auditing of grading, logging, replay, and versioning artifacts, plus adopting four cheap checks (graded fraction, root-span cost aggregation, action provenance tagging, pinned evaluator versions with re-grade diffs). Costs are primarily engineering time to implement reporting and provenance tracking and occasional re-grading compute; no foundation-model training or cluster is required. Failure after adoption includes residual silent instrumentation bugs elsewhere, misinterpretation of published diffs or provenance, and re-grading itself becoming a new, unacknowledged measurement if versions and procedures are not pinned.

The paper documents score corrections that close a 13-point gap by grading unscored episodes, and reorders leaderboards when fixing evaluator bugs; one misread mode check collapses scores by 59 to 82 points.
